description: Controlled vocabulary for the jurisdiction that issues a regulation or standard. Referenced by the 'jurisdiction' field in regulations.json. Levels run from 'international' (standards bodies and multilateral soft law with no independent force of law) down to 'subnational' (a single US state). 'multistate' covers US model-law bodies such as the NAIC whose instruments bind only once a state adopts them. National nodes outside the US (uk, china, singapore, canada) hold thin reference instruments so comparative queries can resolve even before vertical controls cite them.

levels.international: A standards body or multilateral instrument with no independent force of law.
levels.supranational: A treaty-based authority whose instruments bind its member states.
levels.national: A sovereign state or one of its federal agencies.
levels.multistate: A US model-law or coordinating body whose instruments bind only where a state adopts them.
levels.subnational: A single US state or equivalent.

jurisdictions.name: International (standards bodies)
jurisdictions.note: ISO/IEC, IEC, OWASP, MITRE, CIS, CSA, FINOS and similar. Adopted voluntarily or by reference from a binding instrument. Soft-law fora with a distinct issuer identity (OECD) use their own node.

jurisdictions.name: OECD
jurisdictions.note: Intergovernmental soft law. The OECD AI Principles bind no one directly, but supply vocabulary reused by the EU AI Act, NIST AI RMF, and most national strategies.

jurisdictions.name: European Union
jurisdictions.note: Regulations apply directly in member states; directives require transposition.

jurisdictions.name: United States (federal)
jurisdictions.note: Statute, agency rule, supervisory guidance, and executive-branch policy such as OMB memoranda.

jurisdictions.name: United States (multistate model law)
jurisdictions.note: NAIC and similar model-law bodies. Peer to federal statute, not subordinate to it. Instruments bind only where a state adopts them, so a control citing one may be mandatory in some states and advisory in others.

jurisdictions.name: United Kingdom
jurisdictions.note: Pro-innovation regulator-led AI approach rather than a single horizontal AI Act. Sector regulators retain primary enforcement.

jurisdictions.name: People's Republic of China
jurisdictions.note: CAC and related ministry rules on algorithmic recommendation, deep synthesis, and generative AI services.

jurisdictions.name: Singapore
jurisdictions.note: Model AI Governance Framework and related IMDA/PDPC guidance. Voluntary baseline widely cited in Asia-Pacific procurement.

jurisdictions.name: Canada
jurisdictions.note: Federal Directive on Automated Decision-Making for government systems; AIDA remains proposed statute rather than enacted law.
